purpose: Demonstrate a real human-Agent scientific discovery process in which a broad ICU research direction is iteratively developed into multiple evidence-mapped candidates, humans provide clinical and methods feedback, and one purposively selected flagship idea is carried through governed analysis, evidence-bound artifacts, and a bounded manuscript-ready conclusion.
selection_authority: The Agent generates, critiques, revises, and registers candidate ideas across multiple rounds; human clinical and methods reviewers direct the iteration and approve the final flagship idea. The Agent does not autonomously select the research question.
relationship_to_confirmatory_ab: WP5 is a purposively selected descriptive showcase. It is not part of the Heldout27 denominator, does not estimate an idea-landing rate or A-versus-B superiority, and cannot modify or rescue WP2 or WP3 results.

initial_direction_contract.authoring: The study team or an invited clinical collaborator supplies one authentic broad ICU research direction. External authorship is not required because WP5 demonstrates collaborative workflow rather than unbiased case sampling. The manuscript must state whether the direction was internally authored.
forbidden_fields: claim that the case is representative of all possible research directions
initial_direction_contract.contamination_check: Independent evaluators certify before sealing that the initial direction does not reproduce a Dev9, Qualification12, Heldout27, or Formal Safety12 question.
initial_direction_contract.showcase_selection_disclosure: The flagship is purposively selected after outcome-blind feasibility to maximize the chance of an informative end-to-end demonstration. This is permitted because WP5 estimates no success rate, superiority effect, or representative population quantity. The complete append-only discovery trace, selection rationale, internal or external direction authorship, and registered terminal disposition must remain visible.

workflow_stages.required_artifact: immutable initial-direction receipt, role record, and conflict declaration
workflow_stages.gate: The authentic broad direction and iterative discovery contract are sealed and contain no required numeric answer or effect direction.

workflow_stages.required_artifact: versioned query log, retrieval receipts, literature snapshots, inclusion log, and evidence-gap map
workflow_stages.gate: Every literature or metadata claim resolves to a declared query, retrieved source, timestamp, and digest; retrieval completeness is not claimed. New rounds append records and never overwrite earlier evidence maps.

workflow_stages.required_artifact: append-only registry of candidate versions with PICO or equivalent elements, bounded novelty, relevance, feasibility, risks, reviewer feedback, revisions, and rejection reasons
workflow_stages.gate: Multiple generate-critique-revise rounds are allowed within the frozen phase-A budget. Candidates and rejected versions are never deleted; if no defensible candidate exists, the trace records why rather than inventing one.

workflow_stages.required_artifact: clinical and methods feedback records, candidate comparison, decision log, and unresolved reservations
workflow_stages.gate: Humans may request multiple scientific revisions before final lock. Deliberation uses literature, declared nonpatient metadata, and deterministic feasibility summaries, not patient-level outcome results.

workflow_stages.required_artifact: candidate-specific concept map, source-authority audit, WP1-extension receipt, neutral feasibility summary, and draft native-v2 input manifest
workflow_stages.gate: Deterministic feasibility may be checked during discovery without a Provider call or patient-level outcome result. A failed feasibility check may return to the append-only ideation loop within the frozen phase-A budget.

workflow_stages.required_artifact: final selected-idea receipt; locked population, exposure or index, outcome, time origin, estimand, method, missing-data policy, diagnostics, sensitivities, and claim ceiling; native-v2 input manifest; immutable analysis packet
workflow_stages.gate: After deterministic feasibility passes, clinical and methods reviewers approve and lock the final idea, analysis plan, concept map, database, and input before any patient-level outcome analysis. Once phase B is declared, none can be replaced.

workflow_stages.required_artifact: executable code, run receipts, cohort and denominator record, results, diagnostics, sensitivity analyses, and resource receipt
workflow_stages.gate: The locked plan is executed once in fresh context under the frozen release and phase-B budget. No postresult plan change, selective retry, product repair, or substitution of another candidate is allowed for the registered showcase.

workflow_stages.required_artifact: EvidenceStore manifest, artifact digests, figure or table package, bounded interpretation, limitations, manuscript-ready paragraph, and replayable provenance-preserving product demonstration trace
workflow_stages.gate: Every headline number and claim resolves to an artifact. The report identifies the flagship as purposively selected, separates discovery from locked analysis, and stays within the design, data, diagnostics, and literature authority.

two_phase_execution.phase_a_iterative_discovery: I01 through I06 form a bounded iterative human-Agent discovery loop. Provider calls may access only the sealed direction, declared literature retrieval, nonpatient metadata, database capability summaries, and neutral deterministic feasibility receipts. Patient rows, patient-level outcome results, benchmark taskbanks, and repository access are forbidden.
two_phase_execution.interphase_gate: After one idea passes deterministic feasibility, the final idea, plan, concept map, and input are locked and hashed. A passing phase-B declaration permits patient-level outcome analysis. A failed feasibility check before this declaration may return to phase A without erasing any candidate or failure record.
two_phase_execution.phase_b_locked_analysis: I07 through I08 use the same frozen EasyICU release and declared model configuration with only the sealed flagship input packet.
two_phase_execution.postoutcome_boundary: After the first patient-level outcome result is available, any new or materially revised question is exploratory and cannot replace the registered flagship. Confirming such a new question requires a separately versioned case and fresh validation data.
two_phase_execution.derived_artifact_boundary: The append-only candidate registry, final selected idea, approved plan, concept map, and phase-B input are registered outputs of the frozen iterative discovery contract; their hashes are bound in the phase-B declaration.

run_policy.terminal_reporting_rule: Once the phase-B declaration is signed, the registered flagship's terminal disposition is the WP5 result. If it terminates as safe_nonlanding or workflow_failure, that disposition is reported as the WP5 outcome; WP5 may not be withdrawn from the manuscript after phase B is declared.
run_policy.budget_status: Phase-A Provider, retrieval, wall-time, cost, iteration-round, deterministic-feasibility, and human-time ceilings plus phase-B token, wall-time, cost, and compute ceilings must be numerically frozen in the WP5 atomic declarations.

sequence_and_contamination_firewall.sequence: Run WP5 only after every core WP2 and WP3 pair has a terminal immutable receipt. WP5 may occur before or after blinded scoring, but cannot change core artifacts, code, prompts, rubrics, or analyses.
sequence_and_contamination_firewall.release_identity: Use the same immutable EasyICU code, container, owner contracts, and publication gates as the core formal batch. Any product change creates a new descriptive demonstration version and cannot repair the registered showcase.
sequence_and_contamination_firewall.benchmark_firewall: The WP5 runtime cannot read Dev9, Qualification12, Heldout27, Formal Safety12, their rubrics, or their outputs.
sequence_and_contamination_firewall.manuscript_firewall: WP5 findings are reported separately from WP2 effect estimates and cannot redefine the primary endpoint, subgroups, or interpretation.

literature_retrieval_policy.access: Only a declared literature-search and page-retrieval route is allowed during discovery; arbitrary web, repository, email, and messaging access remain denied.
literature_retrieval_policy.reproducibility: Record query strings, databases or APIs, search timestamps, returned identifiers, inclusion decisions, retrieved content digests, unavailable sources, and query revisions across rounds.
literature_retrieval_policy.novelty_boundary: Novelty means not identified as already answered within the bounded retrieved evidence set as of the search timestamp. It is not universal novelty or proof that no prior study exists.

demonstration_package.required_for_showcase: A timestamped event timeline maps the initial direction, every candidate version, literature and feasibility iteration, human decision, final lock, execution, evidence, and reporting event to immutable receipts. Rejected candidates and failed preoutcome feasibility paths remain visible in the discovery trace.
allowed_media: screen recording generated from the real showcase run
manuscript workflow figure derived from the same receipts
prohibited: simulated scientific results presented as real
one-shot autonomous-discovery framing that hides human feedback or prior candidate rounds
postoutcome switching to a more attractive idea or result
UI-only claims without matching run and artifact receipts
demonstration_package.paper_role: The main paper presents the registered flagship case and its terminal disposition. If the case lands, it may be presented as a successful workflow demonstration; otherwise the registered safe_nonlanding or workflow_failure disposition remains reportable. The case-selection and iteration trace must be disclosed, and scientific authority remains with the locked analysis and evidence artifacts.

claim_ceiling: WP5 can demonstrate that one purposively selected, transparently iterated human-Agent case reached an evidence-bound scientific output under the frozen workflow. It cannot estimate an idea-generation or landing rate, establish superior ideation, prove universal novelty, support autonomous-science claims, or generalize scientific validity beyond the showcase.
